articles.title: Are the Knicks ready for what's next? New York's repeat bid begins with nowhere to hide in wide-open NBA
articles.summary: After the parades and the banners and the rings, there's one more reward awaiting the champs: the proverbial bullseye on their back.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Everywhere you looked, it seemed, there they were.

Fresh off the run of a lifetime — a 16-3 sprint through the postseason, headlined by some of the most remarkable blowouts and comebacks in NBA playoff history, capped off by an all-time individual performance in the NBA Finals to clinch the franchise's first NBA championship in 53 years — the New York Knicks spent their summers basking in the afterglow, enjoying the fruits of their labors.

A ticker-tape parade through the Canyon of Heroes in lower Manhattan. Guest spots on "The Tonight Show," "Late Night," "The View," and "Good Morning America." Ceremonial first pitches at Yankee Stadium and Citi Field , and streets renamed in their honor. Places of prominence in the stands at the World Cup and U.S. Open . Featured appearances at both "Saturday Night's Main Event" and "Saturday Night Live."

Jalen Brunson heard MVP chants at City Hall . Karl-Anthony Towns heard "Knicks in five!" during a honeymoon trip to the Serengeti. Mike Brown heard a standing ovation when he and his wife walked into the Polo Bar.

Everywhere the head coach turned, another well-wisher. More congratulations. Another hand to shake.

"I had nowhere to hide," Brown said at the Knicks' media day session last month.

On Tuesday night, the Knicks will experience one final celebration of what they accomplished in June. They'll watch a banner raised to the rafters of Madison Square Garden. They'll receive championship rings laden with enough ice to turn autumn into winter. They'll revel in it all one more time, feeling the adulation of the New York faithful wash over them …

… and then look down from the rafters and see Joel Embiid, LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe and the rest of the Philadelphia 76ers, all champing at the bit for the opportunity to knock the newly anointed kings right off the top of the mountain.

"I mean, obviously, you look at it on paper, and that's a hell of a group," Knicks guard Landry Shamet said at Monday's practice ahead of Tuesday's season opener. "We know that, and I think that's why a lot of our focus has got to be on that, and the ring and the celebration has kind of gotta be secondary. Because our job is our job, and it is 0-0, and I don't think any of us are satisfied with going home with just this championship. We've got things we're still striving toward."

You've surely heard it by now. No NBA champion has repeated since the 2017 and 2018 Golden State Warriors. The last Eastern Conference champion to return to the Finals the following year? The LeBron-led Cleveland Cavaliers that did battle with those Dubs.

Such is life in Adam Silver's Parity of Opportunity Era, a moment in NBA history in which it seems champions are built to be broken. We can't pin this entirely on the advent of aprons, though; the head that wears the crown has always been heavy.

After the parades and the TV appearances and the ovations and the banners and the rings, there's one more reward awaiting a champion: the proverbial bullseye on your back. You survived the 100-game marathon to reach the top of the mountain and hoist the trophy? Congratulations. All your hard work has earned you is … more hard work. Harder work. Every opponent's best shot, every single night.

"To repeat is gonna take an even higher sense of discipline and execution, and we're gonna have to even be better than what we showed in the playoffs," Towns said. "So, all of us are aware that we're gonna have to bring a whole other level to the table if we expect to have a chance to repeat."

Coming off their fever-dream postseason, the Knicks awake in a conference that has risen to meet them. After taking on the new-look Sixers on ring night, the Knicks head to Boston to play a Celtics team featuring a healthy Jayson Tatum, new arrival Paul George and old pal Mitchell Robinson. Then, it's back to Manhattan for a visit from the Orlando Magic, led by new head coach Sean Sweeney, who just four months ago was devising schemes to try to stifle New York as the defensive coordinator in San Antonio.

Two nights later, the Pistons come to MSG, eager to pick up where they left off last season, when they won all three of their regular-season meetings with the Knicks — by a total of 84 points . In early November, they'll have a pair of meetings with the Cleveland Cavaliers, whom they swept in the Eastern Conference finals, and who bring back a core of four All-Stars — Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen — while adding a plug-and-play big wing in Peyton Watson.

They'll renew unpleasantries with the Indiana Pacers, the last team to beat the Knicks in a playoff series, who are eager to get back up to speed now that Tyrese Haliburton is back and in full form. They'll face off with the Toronto Raptors, who added All-NBA game-breaker Kawhi Leonard to their playoff core. They'll welcome the Miami Heat, who dealt for former MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo.

Nowhere to run to, baby; nowhere to hide.

"The first couple of weeks or whatever of the season is going to show us who we are and where we are," Brunson said.

On the bright side, the Knicks should enter this season with a pretty good handle on who they can be and where they can go.

The loss of reserve center Robinson, who went to rival Boston in free agency after Knicks owner James L. Dolan made it clear he would not allow his front office to spend past the second apron line to fully run back the title rotation, figures to hurt, even if veteran replacement Andre Drummond can carry his strong preseason form into the games that count. So, too, could the overarching unpleasantness surrounding stalled talks on contract extensions for Towns, Hart and reserve guard Miles "Deuce" McBride — though all parties involved insist they're entering the season focused on competing, producing and repeating rather than on the ins and outs of their negotiation frustrations.

Even without Robinson, though, nine of New York's 10 most frequently used players from the title team return, accounting for more than 92% of their postseason minutes — a considerable level of continuity, cohesion and shared experience from which to draw as the group starts the climb anew.

"I think what's most important is that, I mean, last year we took everything one day at a time," Brunson said. "We were talking about — obviously, the topic was getting back to the conference finals [where they'd been eliminated by the Pacers in 2025 ] and trying to advance. And I think for us now, the way we approached it last year was to take it one day at a time, every single day. Obviously, we know what it takes, but just going into this with the same mindset for this journey. Even though it's a new journey, it's a different journey. The approach has to be the same, if not better."

Throughout training camp and the preseason, Brown has preached that message, emphasizing that the only way for the Knicks to hope to achieve the same results they did last season is to maintain the same zealous adherence to the step-by-step, brick-by-brick approach that produced them — to the collective standard of sacrifice, connectivity, competition and shared belief that brought them to the promised land.

"We can't afford any slippage in our process," Brown said. "We're going to have our ups and downs. We have to understand that the media scrutiny and the public scrutiny is going to come. It is what it is, and there's going to be a lot of comparisons, but we have no control over that. The only thing we can control is: what's our daily habits? Where is our focus and our energy going every day?"

It looked like it might take some time to re-establish those habits, that focus and that energy. Brown didn't ask his players to get back into the Knicks training facility until after Labor Day , giving them some extra time to decompress after the championship run and subsequent celebration. The early preseason returns didn't look particularly promising, with the Knicks dropping their first four games, and Brown pointedly calling out their lack of competitive toughness in the preseason opener against Philly.

"What bothers me is our lack of physicality throughout the ball game, and that's the whole roster up and down," Brown told reporters . "We weren't great on the ball physically and we weren't great with our defensive positioning physically. [...] I can't help with the physicality. That they've gotta find individually, which will then turn into collectively, and that's how you find minutes. That's how you make the team."

Which, as Brown made clear, was not a guarantee for everybody past New York's high-priced, big-name title core.

"I specifically went down the line talking about Jalen, Mikal [Bridges], OG [Anunoby], KAT and Josh [Hart]," Brown told reporters during the preseason. "I said, 'Those five, they gonna play. If they do something wrong, I'm gonna get on them and we're gonna figure it out, but they still gonna play.' I said, 'Everybody else in this gym, you fighting. You fighting either to make the team or you fighting for minutes.'

"I said, 'Look around. This is not just because we won last year. This has nothing to do with last year's team. Those five guys are the same. But everybody — this is a new year, a new team. We gotta look forward. Every day, it's a competition.'"

With that competitive expectation clearly communicated and established, and with so much talent staring at them up and down the Eastern Conference standings, the Knicks enter the new season with no illusions about being able to rest on their laurels.

"It can be human nature to relax a little bit [...] anybody that works in the building, as a player, as a coach, as a fan, you can relax after having a lot of success," Bridges told reporters during the preseason. "It's difficult to do something great and continue to try to get better. That's our goal."

"There's no relaxation whatsoever," Brunson told reporters at Knicks practice on Monday. "None. I think every year, it's a new year to kind of attack something. When people say we're 'defending the title,' I mean, that's one way to look at it. But it's something we won, we've put it in our past, and now we're just trying to attack another."

That's the mentality the Knicks appear to be bringing into the new campaign: looking to attack, rather than defend. And if a preseason-finale dress-rehearsal win over the Raptors — one in which Brunson led five Knicks in double-figures, Towns flirted with a triple-double, and New York had 35 assists on 43 made field goals — is any indication, Brown's club might be ready to resume its pursuit.

"Everyone loves to compete, so as the season goes on, yeah, we'll be hunted," Anunoby said. "But we're going to be hunting other teams, as well."

The hunt begins Tuesday: for proper execution on offense and the right attention to detail on defense; for the willingness to be honest with and accountable to one another; for the relentless commitment to Brown's standard; for a new beginning, a new challenge, a new journey.

"I would say most of us, if not all of us, have turned the page already," Brunson said Monday. "I think tomorrow is just something we can reflect on and understand what we did. But for the most part, we've all turned the page."

The banner rises. The rings get tucked away. The ball goes up, and everybody's once again staring at a blank page. How are the Knicks going to fill it?

"At the end of the day," Hart said, "we write our own history."

articles.title: In 2024, Jalen Brunson signed a $156.5 million Knicks deal instead of waiting for $113 million more; two years later, he became an NBA champion
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson had a chance to pursue a five-year, $269.1 million contract in 2025.
articles.body: Jalen Brunson had a chance to pursue a five-year, $269.1 million contract in 2025. Instead, the Knicks guard signed a four-year, $156.5 million extension in 2024. The projected difference was roughly $113 million in potential earnings. After two years, Brunson led the Knicks to their first NBA championship since 1973 and won the 2026 Finals MVP award.His decision also gave the team more financial flexibility to build its roster. But the $113 million figure does not represent a confirmed loss, as Brunson can pursue another major contract under future eligibility rules Why Jalen Brunson signed a $156.5 million contract with the Knicks in 2024Brunson agreed to the extension on July 12, 2024, after the best regular season of his NBA career. He averaged 28.7 points and 6.7 assists per game in 2023-24, earned his first All-Star selection and made the All-NBA Second Team. He also finished fifth in MVP voting. His scoring helped the Knicks finish second in the Eastern Conference and reach the conference semifinals before losing to the Indiana Pacers in seven games.The extension came with a clear financial trade-off. Brunson could sign for $156.5 million over four years in 2024. By waiting until 2025, he could have pursued a five-year contract projected at $269.1 million. ESPN reported that the difference in potential guaranteed money was approximately $113 million.The larger deal was possible because the NBA's contract rules would have allowed the Knicks to offer him a more lucrative maximum contract after another season. By signing early, Brunson secured his extension before reaching that point.His decision also helped New York manage its payroll. The Knicks had acquired Mikal Bridges from the Brooklyn Nets in a trade that involved five first-round draft picks. They had also re-signed forward OG Anunoby to a five-year contract worth a reported $212.5 million. Both moves increased the team's financial commitments as the front office tried to build a roster around Brunson.Brunson's extension helped the Knicks stay below the NBA's second-apron threshold, which imposes additional restrictions on teams that spend beyond it. Those restrictions can limit trades and other roster-building options. His contract gave New York more room to manage its commitments while retaining important players.His father, Rick Brunson, worked as a Knicks assistant coach, while team president Leon Rose had previously represented Jalen as his agent. Brunson had joined New York in 2022 on a four-year, $104 million contract after leaving the Dallas Mavericks. By 2024, he had developed into an All-NBA guard and the centre of the Knicks' plans.The extension did not guarantee that New York would win a championship. The front office still needed to assemble the right supporting cast, and the players had to perform in the playoffs. But Brunson's willingness to sign early gave the team additional financial flexibility at a critical point in its development. How the Knicks turned that flexibility into a championshipThe Knicks continued to build around Brunson after the extension. Bridges joined Anunoby, Josh Hart and other key players in a group designed to compete in the Eastern Conference. New York later added Karl-Anthony Towns, giving Brunson another high-level offensive option.Brunson remained the team's primary ball-handler and scorer. His ability to create shots, attack defenders and organise the offence made him central to New York's postseason success.The payoff arrived in June 2026. The Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 4-1 in the NBA Finals securing their first championship since 1973. Brunson scored 45 points in the decisive Game 5, which New York won 94-90. He averaged 32.6 points per game in the Finals and received the Bill Russell NBA Finals MVP award.The final game showcased the scoring ability that had made Brunson one of the league's leading guards. He scored 15 points in the fourth quarter as the Knicks recovered from a deficit to secure the title. His 45-point performance also set a Knicks record for points in an NBA Finals game.The championship ended a 53-year wait for New York. The franchise had reached the Finals before, but its previous championship came in 1973. Brunson's arrival in 2022 had helped change the team's fortunes, and his performances in the 2026 playoffs placed him at the centre of its title run.The financial decision from 2024 was only one part of that success. New York still needed strong performances from its supporting cast, effective coaching and successful roster moves. However, Brunson's contract helped the organisation manage its payroll while adding players around its leading guard.Jalen Brunson’s contract and the Knicks’ championship futureBrunson enters the 2026-27 season as the reigning NBA Finals MVP and the leader of the defending champions. His 2026 postseason performance strengthened his standing in New York, where the franchise had spent decades trying to return to the top of the league.His contract remains relevant as the Knicks manage a roster with several expensive players. articles.title: Los Sixers sacuden el juego de tronos de la NBA
articles.standfirst: Alzan el telón del nuevo curso desafiando a Knicks, Thunder y Spurs con intención de cambiar el orden establecido. Van a por el anillo con sus cuatro fantásticos
articles.summary: Alzan el telón del nuevo curso desafiando a Knicks, Thunder y Spurs con intención de cambiar el orden establecido. Van a por el anillo con sus cuatro fantásticos
articles.body: Oklahoma City Thunder y San Antonio Spurs arrancan como favoritos en los pronósticos para conquistar el anillo de campeón de la NBA que esta noche alza el telón de una nueva temporada, , pero todas las miradas se dirigen a unos Philadelphia 76ers que han dinamitado el mercado con una concentración de estrellas capaz de alterar la jerarquía de la liga. Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, LeBron James y Jaylen Brown forman un cuarteto de lujo con el que Philadelphia aspira a dejar de ser una promesa incumplida para convertirse en el gran aspirante al anillo. El desafío es mayúsculo: destronar a los campeones Knicks, adelantar al resto de favoritos y demostrar que el talento, cuando se pone al servicio de una idea colectiva, puede cambiar la historia. Pocas plantillas pueden reunir semejante combinación de recursos. Embiid es la referencia interior; Maxey, el acelerador ofensivo; LeBron, el cerebro que ordena el juego, y Brown, una amenaza física y anotadora de primer nivel. Philadelphia dispone de estrellas capaces de resolver partidos por diferentes vías, una ventaja especialmente valiosa cuando llegan las eliminatorias y las defensas rivales cierran espacios. La gran pregunta es si todas aceptarán compartir el protagonismo. Si encuentran el equilibrio, los Sixers tendrán argumentos para discutir el campeonato a cualquier rival. New York, con Jalen Brunson al frente y Karl-Anthony Towns como socio ofensivo, representa uno de los grandes obstáculos para Philadelphia. Los Knicks cuentan con continuidad, carácter y una estructura competitiva, pero ahora deben medirse con una plantilla que ha elevado el listón del talento individual. Los Celtics de Jayson Tatum, los Cavaliers de Donovan Mitchell y los Pistons de Cade Cunningham completan un Este en el que los Sixers aspiran a imponer su candidatura. La presión recae sobre Philadelphia: su inversión en estrellas exige resultados. La historia se ha encargado de demostrar en muchas ocasiones que reunir figuras no garantiza levantar el trofeo. En el pasado fueron muchos los 'Big Three' o 'Big Four' ilustres que se pegaron el batacazo. El entrenador de los Sixers, Nick Nurse, deberá encajar el dominio interior de Embiid, la velocidad de Maxey, la capacidad organizativa de LeBron y la agresividad ofensiva de Brown. El reparto de tiros, la gestión de los minutos y la responsabilidad en los finales apretados serán determinantes. Philadelphia tiene potencial para construir uno de los ataques más temibles que se haya visto nunca en la NBA, pero sólo con eso no le va a dar para iniciar una dinastía, que es con lo que sueñan sus aficionados con esa nómina de estrellas. Necesita defender con intensidad y encontrar una identidad que vaya más allá de sus individualidades. El anillo se gana como equipo. Los Thunder parten con la vitola de favoritos gracias a un bloque consolidado y al liderazgo de Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, una estrella que combina eficacia anotadora y sangre fría en los momentos decisivos. Oklahoma City representa el modelo de equipo construido con continuidad y equilibrio, precisamente el examen que deberá superar Philadelphia si quiere convertir su colección de estrellas en una candidatura campeona. Los Sixers pueden tener más nombres de relumbrón; los Thunder quieren demostrar que la química sigue siendo el mejor argumento. San Antonio se presenta como otro gran aspirante gracias a Victor Wembanyama, cuyo impacto defensivo y crecimiento ofensivo le convierten en una figura diferencial. Los Spurs representan el futuro, con un núcleo joven y margen para seguir mejorando; Philadelphia apuesta por la experiencia y el talento inmediato. El contraste convierte a ambos proyectos en dos de los grandes focos de la temporada. Si los Sixers quieren conquistar la NBA, deberán estar preparados para enfrentarse a una generación que no piensa esperar su turno. Denver confía en la inteligencia y versatilidad de Nikola Jokic; Minnesota, en la explosividad de Anthony Edwards; los Lakers, en el talento de Luka Doncic; Houston, en la experiencia de Kevin Durant, y Golden State, en la magia de Stephen Curry. Todos tienen argumentos para complicar la carrera por el título. Philadelphia, sin embargo, puede convertirse en la referencia contra la que se mida el resto de aspirantes: si su superequipo funciona, cada candidato tendrá que encontrar una fórmula para frenar su arsenal ofensivo. Los Cavaliers necesitan que Donovan Mitchell marque diferencias en las eliminatorias; los Pistons, que Cade Cunningham confirme su crecimiento, y los Celtics, que Jayson Tatum recupere su mejor nivel. Pero los Sixers han cambiado la conversación. Su plantilla les obliga a aspirar a las primeras posiciones y convierte cada enfrentamiento directo en una prueba de su capacidad para dominar la conferencia. Philadelphia ya no quiere conformarse con competir: pretende imponer su autoridad y llegar a las Finales como el gran representante del Este. La salud decidirá hasta dónde pueden llegar los Sixers. Su talento es indiscutible, pero su mayor amenaza puede estar en la disponibilidad de Embiid (32 años), proclive a las lesiones, y LeBron (41 años), que deberá administrar el desgaste. La profundidad del equipo y su capacidad para resistir las lesiones marcarán la diferencia entre una candidatura real y una decepción. Si llegan en buenas condiciones a los playoffs, Philadelphia tendrá recursos para desafiar a los Thunder, los Spurs y cualquier rival que se cruce en su camino hacia el anillo. Thunder y Spurs cuentan con el respaldo de los pronósticos, y Knicks, Celtics, Nuggets y Wolves mantienen sus opciones. Pero los Sixers han conseguido algo fundamental antes del primer salto inicial: convertirse en uno de los grandes protagonistas de la temporada. Embiid, Maxey, LeBron y Brown reúnen talento suficiente para desafiar el orden establecido. Ahora les toca demostrar que pueden transformar los focos, las expectativas y los nombres en victorias. La NBA tiene favoritos, pero Philadelphia quiere tener la última palabra.

articles.title: All the ways Angel Reese dominated Game 2 as Dream even WNBA Finals with Valkyries
articles.summary: Drives, dump-offs, putbacks, bullying on the block, pick-and-roll play — Reese would not be denied in Game 2.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — During pregame warmups ahead of Game 2, Angel Reese went through a little bit of everything. Top-of-key jumpers. Take a few steps back , above-the-break 3s.

It's time for Around The World, now — 3s from the corner, the wing, above the break, the opposite wing, and finishing with the opposite corner. It's drive time, working on contested finishes after attacking from the elbow. Then it's time for reverse finishes.

Reese will briefly look around the court in between drills, but she's ultimately locked in. No frills, no distractions; just focused prep with a little more weight on her shoulders.

There's pressure on the Dream to steal a road win, especially after "letting one slip away," in Reese's words. A 68-64 Game 1 loss could've easily been a two-possession win had their execution not faltered. Reese took her own share of accountability after Game 1. An 11-point first quarter ultimately ended in a 14-point performance, her involvement and production waning in the second half. It wasn't anything the Valkyries did, per Reese; she simply wasn't aggressive enough. Didn't do enough.

"I'm definitely going to do a better job of that, next game."

Boy, did she, lifting her team to a convincing 79-65 win in Game 2.

It takes just 46 seconds for Reese to score her first basket in the contest. She trails in transition following the first of Rhyne Howard's WNBA Finals record six steals, eventually gets the rock above the break against Cecilia Zandalasini — funny enough, she also gave up the opening bucket in Game 1 — and wins with a jab-and-drive similar to her pregame work.

That's all it takes for the tone to be set.

Then it's a putback following a Howard miss, after another steal. A double-PnR rep with Jordin Canada at the helm that leads to a layup against Laeticia Amihere — a subtle Game 1 hero due to her defensive work on Reese, but that wouldn't carry over on Monday night.

An elbow flash to set up an immediate drive and drawn foul against Aminata Gueye, one of the surprise rotational stories of the postseason. That sends Reese to the line, which culminates in a healthy back-and-forth that ends with Reese telling Gueye that she can't, um, mess with her .

It's a similar script in the second quarter. A transition basket less than a minute in. Another attack off an elbow flash, this time against Amihere. Amihere is bumped back a few inches on the drive; Tiffany Hayes, trying to blindside Reese with a steal, trips during the attempt. The shot and Hayes fall at nearly the same time.

Drives. Dump-offs. Putbacks. Bullying on the block. Pick-and-roll play. Reese just doesn't stop.

(As an aside: whew, was it refreshing to see her screening perk up. After making contact on 44.4% of her on-ball screens in Game 1, it skyrocketed to 74.2% in Game 2. The team as a whole — from 39.5% to 68.6% — made a massive step there.)

It isn't a perfect affair. Kiah Stokes blocks Reese on multiple trips. Kaila Charles forces a tie-up. It doesn't matter.

And when it feels like things are getting quiet on the Reese front in the third quarter, risking a repeat of Game 1's low-involvement frame, she's there with another reminder.

A catch in transition, a small cross to her left, and a contested finish over a backpedaling Stokes for an and-one. Then, the proclamation, twice: give me the [redacted] ball.

Reese keeps coming. Keeps scoring. Keeps drawing fouls, keeps the pressure on. Keeps her word — I won't let my teammates down again.

The end result, punctuated by yet another postseason triple — Reese is now 6-of-15 from deep during her inaugural playoff run and, as my teammate Cassandra Negley pointed out , the Dream are undefeated in the games Reese has made one — was a win, and a history-making performance. For Reese, the former matters a lot more than the latter.

Still: 30 points, 16 rebounds (4 offensive rebounds), 3 assists, 1 steal and 2 blocks is the stuff of legend.

Reese is one of six players in WNBA history to have a 30-15 game in the playoffs. She's one of three players to do so in the Finals. She's the youngest player to accomplish either.

Basketball-Reference has a box score metric called "Game Score," which uses a formula to determine the most prolific games. The Valkyries, a historically good defense, simply haven't allowed a bunch of great individual performances this year.

Only 13 times has a player logged a Game Score north of 20 this season (regular season + playoffs), the fewest allowed by a team all year.

It's fitting that it's taken, well, historic performances to knock off the Valkyries this postseason. The top game against them? Arike Ogunbowale's 45-point, record-setting masterpiece. Next on the list? Reese's 30-16-3-1-2 masterpiece from Monday night.

Zoom out, and the Dream have ultimately gotten a road split as the series shifts back to Atlanta. Shifts to State Farm Arena, a larger venue that Reese's presence dictates as a home. The Valkyries will go back to the drawing board, looking to showcase better ball control (18 turnovers, tied for their season-high) and ultimately open things up offensively.

In the meantime, we should sit with this Reese performance. It's not every night that you see history made; you should appreciate it in real time.

articles.title: Latest Ticket Prices for Knicks vs. LeBron James' 76ers Reveal Staggering Cost to Get Into MSG
articles.summary: On the heels of the most-expensive NBA Finals in history, the get-in price for the New York Knicks' opener against LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden is also going to cost a small fortune.
articles.body:
On the heels of the most-expensive NBA Finals in history, the get-in price for the New York Knicks' opener against LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden is also going to cost a small fortune.

Ahead of Tuesday's opener between the Sixers and Knicks at MSG, the get-in price on various ticket resellers ranges from $1,865 to over $32,000.

Sixers Out to Spoil Knicks' Ring Night 😈

TickPick.com has the cheapest available tickets for $1,865 in section 418 row six, which is the very top-tier in the arena. It also has the most-expensive listing at $32,354 for a seat in row A, section 6D. There are three listings at more than $20,000 on the side.

The Rate Your Seats website notes seats between rows five through seven in most of the 400-level sections at MSG have an obstructed view.

StubHub.com has nine different listings of tickets for at least $10,000. The most expensive in the group is up for sale at $22,305 located in the third row of section seven behind one of the baskets.

SeatGeek has the smallest range of prices, but there is still a gap of nearly $10,000 between the cheapest ticket in section 225 and section 416.

To compare Tuesday night to the NBA Finals, Games 3 and 4 at Madison Square Garden had get-in prices starting at $11,000 and $13,000, respectively. So this game is, by that standard, more affordable for average fans.

Per Tania Ganguli of the New York Times , the cheapest ticket for the Knicks' season opener on Tuesday is $786 more than the cheapest ticket for the 2025-26 opener against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Not surprisingly, the Knicks have, by far, the highest median ticket price for home games this season at $226. The Los Angeles Lakers are a distant second at $113.

Interestingly, the Sixers—even with the addition of James—are fifth. They trail the Knicks, Lakers, Boston Celtics and Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Knicks will get their championship rings on Tuesday night before tipping off their season against the Sixers at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: "NBA Europa empezará en 2027, haya o no acuerdo con la Euroliga"
articles.standfirst: Mark Tatum, Comisionado Adjunto y Director de Operaciones de la NBA, presenta la nueva temporada y habla del proyecto de la Liga en Europa
articles.summary: Mark Tatum, Comisionado Adjunto y Director de Operaciones de la NBA, presenta la nueva temporada y habla del proyecto de la Liga en Europa
articles.body: No hay arranque de la temporada en la NBA en la que no haya una intervención a nivel internacional de alguno de los hombres más poderosos de la Liga. Es la forma institucional de dar por inaugurada la temporada en la mejor Liga del mundo. En esta ocasión fue Mark Tatum, Comisionado Adjunto y Director de Operaciones de la NBA, el que se encargó de hablar con la prensa internacional sobre el estreno de una nueva campaña aprovechando que este martes se disputan los primeros partidos de la Liga regular. Pero, obviamente, con prensa europea, gran parte de las preguntas a Tatum se centraron en el proyecto que la NBA quiere establecer en el Viejo Continente. Tatum confirmó que las negociaciones con la Euroliga siguen pero que el lanzamiento de la competición para 2027 seguirá su curso haya o no acuerdo. "Tenemos mucho trabajo por hacer, pero estamos avanzando rápidamente y no estamos bajando el ritmo en absoluto", dijo Tatum sobre el proyecto de NBA Europe. "Estamos en proceso de cerrar los acuerdos y pronto lanzaremos franquicias. Las conversaciones con la Euroliga continúan, pero la NBA tiene preparado su propio plan", y añadió, "Este es un momento histórico y tenemos que hacerlo bien". El Vicecomisionado habló de la importancia del proyecto de NBA Europa: "No se trata solo de una temporada ni de poner en marcha una nueva liga; se trata de replantear todo el ecosistema del baloncesto europeo, cimentado sobre una base basada en el mérito que otorga a cada aficionado y a cada club de Europa el derecho a soñar. La estructura actual confunde al aficionado europeo con la Euroliga, la Basketball Champions League, la Eurocup, la FIBA Europe Cup, las competiciones domñesticas... Queremos establecer una estructura mucho más sencilla". Preguntado sobre el reciente anuncio de la Euroliga sobre su plan económico para los próximos años. Tatum dijo: "Ese anuncio no afecta nuestro proyecto. Nuestro modelo proporcionará a los clubes un camino mucho más rápido hacia la rentabilidad. He leído informes sobre equipos de la Euroliga que actualmente no gozan de estabilidad financiera; según nuestras proyecciones, un equipo con plaza fija en nuestra liga alcanzará, de media, la rentabilidad en su tercer año. También he visto las cifras que la Euroliga prevé invertir o redistribuir entre sus clubes. Nuestras proyecciones indican que triplicaremos esas estimaciones, con una distribución total a lo largo de diez años que ascenderá a miles —e incluso decenas de miles— de millones de dólares, destinados a revertir en los clubes y garantizar su estabilidad financiera". Tatum no quiso hablar de fechas ni calendarios al respecto: "No hay un cronograma para los anuncios; estamos trabajando para tener la liga lista dentro de un año", confirmando que, haya o no acuerdo con la Euroliga la NBA Europe verá la luz en octubre de 2027: "Seguimos en discusiones activas con la Euroliga. Creemos que todas las partes deben estar alineadas, pero también somos realistas. Estamos listos para proceder con la FIBA y nuestros socios si es necesario". Mark Tatum habló también del emergente baloncesto internacional cada vez más presente en la NBA: "En 1992, cuando el Dream Team jugó en Barcelona, teníamos menos de 30 jugadores internacionales. Ahora hemos cudruplicado esa cifra (125). Aquel equipo inspipró a jugadores como Tony Parker o Pau Gasol que a su vez han inspirado a otros en todo el mundo".

articles.title: WNBA tells Congress that Enes Kanter Freedom, Royce White are ‘both men’ in eligibility dispute
articles.summary: Cathy Engelbert told Congress that Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White are "both men" but declined to define "women" under WNBA eligibility rules.
articles.body: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert told Republican lawmakers that former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White are ineligible to play in the league because they are "both men," responding to a congressional inquiry without supplying the definition of "women" that lawmakers had requested. "With respect to your questions regarding eligibility, only women are eligible to play in the WNBA and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men," Engelbert wrote in the Oct. 16 response. The letter, which is dated Oct. 16, was provided to OutKick by the America First Policy Institute (AFPI), which represents Freedom. The letter answered a Sept. 17 inquiry from Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Ind., and four other House Republicans about eligibility, player safety and confrontations with fans. Freedom and White had announced plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft while saying they identify as women. GOP CONGRESSMAN PRESSES WNBA TO DEFINE ‘WOMEN’ AFTER ENES KANTER FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE RULED INELIGIBLE The lawmakers asked how the league defines "women" under Article XIII, Section 1(a) of its collective bargaining agreement, and why the two former NBA players had been deemed ineligible. That provision of the 2026 agreement states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." It does not define the term in that eligibility provision. Stutzman welcomed Engelbert’s statement as an acknowledgment of a distinction based on biological sex. "The WNBA has just taken the first step in defining what a woman is for the sports community," Stutzman said in a statement. "By clearly labeling Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White as men they have acknowledged that identifying as a woman does not change basic human biology." WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT SENDS TRANS INCLUSION MEMO AFTER ENES FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE ANNOUNCEMENTS Engelbert’s letter did not announce a new eligibility rule or spell out a broader policy governing transgender athletes. Freedom, meanwhile, argued that the response left unanswered the central question of what standards the WNBA applies when deciding who qualifies to compete. "Cathy Engelbert cannot clearly define what a woman is, but she's absolutely certain that I'm a man," Freedom told OutKick. "I mean, how does that make sense? Who gets to decide? Who has the authority to determine whether someone is a woman?" "So if the league is still working through these questions, how can its commissioner be so certain about my eligibility without explaining the standards that she's applying?" he added. Asked whether he believed Engelbert had misgendered him in her letter to Congress, Freedom answered, "Yes, 100%." "I just want her to respect my identity because I am telling you that I identify as a woman," he said. Freedom said his effort to join the league is intended to push it to adopt an explicit requirement limiting participation to biological females. He acknowledged that determining someone’s identity and determining eligibility for women’s sports may involve different decisions. "This is bigger than one basketball player," he said. "I mean, who gets to determine someone's identity? The individual, the commissioner, the medical professional, or a committee or a task force?" "And who gets to determine eligibility to compete in women's category?" he continued. "So those may be different decisions, but the WNBA needs to explain where it draws the line." The debate over the league’s eligibility standards intensified this summer after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham voiced support for excluding transgender girls and women from female sports. Her comments drew both support and criticism, including rallies during the Fever’s road trips. Some players and coaches publicly supported transgender inclusion. Freedom has pointed to Golden State Valkyries player Gabby Williams’ support for transgender athletes as the inspiration for his own effort to enter the WNBA. In August, a league task force of team presidents and general managers discussed transgender participation along with online abuse directed at players. The task force was an existing anti-hate committee, rather than a group created solely to determine eligibility. At the time, the league said there were no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA and condemned attempts to use the subject to demean or marginalize others. It said discussions with league stakeholders would continue in the coming weeks and months. Freedom questioned how the league’s ongoing discussions fit with Engelbert’s definitive statement about him and White. "So what about the task force?" he said. "If the task force itself has not reached a clear definition, why is the commissioner making such a definitive statement?" CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Eligibility was only one part of the lawmakers’ inquiry. Their September letter also challenged the league’s response to physical play, including incidents involving Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington and Cunningham, and sought an explanation of its handling of confrontations between players and spectators. In her response, Engelbert defended the league’s officiating and disciplinary processes. She said officials enforce the rules during games, while WNBA League Basketball Operations reviews games afterward, including atypical or overly physical plays. The league can then upgrade fouls or impose discipline. "In all instances the League seeks to apply its rules and relevant disciplinary processes consistently for all players, coaches, and officials," Engelbert wrote. On fan conduct, the commissioner said spectators must follow the WNBA’s code of conduct and can be ejected for violations. She said the league and its teams seek to enforce that code consistently. The lawmakers had specifically cited Sky guard Natasha Cloud’s confrontation with Freedom during an Aug. 23 game against the Fever at Wintrust Arena. They questioned why Cloud had not received punishment while Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton received a five-game suspension following a separate confrontation with fans. Engelbert’s response did not specifically explain the different outcomes involving Cloud and Keaton. Freedom was ejected from the Chicago game and subsequently banned from Sky home games at Wintrust Arena. He later filed a lawsuit alleging that his First Amendment rights had been violated. Sky owner Michael Alter disputed that account, saying security removed Freedom because of his conduct, rather than his speech. Stutzman said he continued to have concerns beyond the eligibility issue. The national anthem has become another point of criticism during the WNBA Finals. Players from the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries left the court before the anthem during the opening two games and returned after it concluded. "While this is a step in the right direction, the alarming disrespect the WNBA still has for their fans and our national anthem needs to be corrected," he said. articles.title: Sergio de Larrea ya mira a Luka Doncic: "Es mi X en el calendario"
articles.standfirst: El base español, que debutará con los Dallas Mavericks, atiende a 'Otra Ronda' de Radio MARCA en vísperas del inicio de la temporada
articles.summary: El base español, que debutará con los Dallas Mavericks, atiende a 'Otra Ronda' de Radio MARCA en vísperas del inicio de la temporada
articles.body: La NBA levanta el telón esta noche y Sergio de Larrea está preparado para afrontar uno de los grandes retos de su carrera. El base español debutará en la mejor liga del mundo con los Dallas Mavericks, una franquicia con la que se siente identificado y en la que compartirá vestuario con estrellas como Kyrie Irving y con Santi Aldama, uno de sus grandes apoyos en esta nueva aventura. En la víspera de su estreno, el jugador atendió a 'Otra Ronda', el programa de Radio MARCA presentado por Carlos Vicente Gómez, 'Chitu', junto al especialista en baloncesto de la emisora, Carlos Santos. En una conversación distendida, De Larrea mostró la tranquilidad con la que afronta el salto a la NBA, sin perder de vista el trabajo diario y la necesidad de adaptarse a una competición que exige un nivel físico y mental extraordinario. "Estoy contento con la oportunidad, tranquilo. La verdad es que esperaba algo así y mentalmente me he ido preparando estos últimos años para lo que me podía encontrar aquí", explicó. Uno de los nombres propios de la entrevista fue el de Santi Aldama. El jugador español se ha convertido en una figura de referencia para De Larrea desde su llegada a Estados Unidos, tanto dentro como fuera de la pista. Su experiencia en la liga está siendo clave para ayudarle a entender las particularidades de la competición y afrontar los primeros pasos de su carrera en la NBA. "Me ha ayudado un montón, fuera de la pista y dentro de la pista. Me comparte sus experiencias, lo que ha vivido, que es muy necesario aquí. La verdad es que es un ángel caído del cielo que me haya venido Santi aquí a Dallas", reconoció. Otro de los grandes atractivos de su nueva etapa será compartir equipo con Kyrie Irving, uno de los bases más talentosos de los últimos años. De Larrea no escondió la admiración que sentía por él antes de llegar a Dallas, aunque ahora ya tiene la oportunidad de conocerlo desde dentro y competir a su lado. "Al principio era más un ídolo, verlo jugar. Creo que es un jugador muy especial", señaló sobre Irving. "Ahora ya es como un compañero, un compañero que te intenta ayudar, que te lleva al máximo en todos los entrenamientos y que te mete más canastas que el resto también en los entrenamientos", añadió entre risas. Preguntado por los aspectos que más necesita mejorar en su adaptación a la NBA, el base señaló el apartado físico como una de sus principales prioridades. El ritmo de juego, la fortaleza de los rivales y la variedad de perfiles a los que tendrá que defender le obligan a seguir evolucionando. "Físicamente creo que es el número uno para intentar adaptarme lo mejor posible a los físicos de la liga", explicó. La nutrición es otro de los aspectos que cuida desde hace tiempo. De Larrea reconoció que siempre ha tenido presente la importancia de la alimentación y que le gusta cocinar, hasta el punto de mencionar el risotto entre sus especialidades El aterrizaje de De Larrea en Dallas no es fruto de una decisión precipitada. El jugador recordó el recorrido de las últimas temporadas, en las que ha acumulado experiencias importantes con Valencia Basket y la selección española antes de dar el salto definitivo. "Siempre ha sido tender más a la paciencia", explicó sobre su trayectoria. A su juicio, el desarrollo mental, físico y deportivo que ha experimentado en los últimos años era necesario para llegar preparado a un entorno completamente diferente. Las experiencias vividas en Valencia, desde ganar títulos hasta disputar una Final Four y afrontar también derrotas dolorosas, le han permitido adquirir herramientas para competir al máximo nivel. "Creo que necesitaba ese desarrollo tanto mental, físico como también de juego y de vivir experiencias", resumió. Más allá del baloncesto, De Larrea mantiene otra faceta que le define: su interés por los estudios. El base confirmó que continúa con su formación universitariay que se encuentra entre primero y segundo curso, aunque ahora tendrá que comprobar cómo puede compaginarla con las exigencias de su nueva vida en Estados Unidos. "Voy a intentar seguir haciéndolo y, si no puedo, ya veré qué puedo hacer", explicó. Los viajes y las horas de hotel se convierten en oportunidades para avanzar con los estudios y aprovechar los tiempos muertos de la temporada. Una muestra más de la disciplina con la que intenta gestionar una carrera profesional que acaba de abrirle las puertas de la NBA. Si hay un encuentro que De Larrea espera con especial ilusión, es el que le permitirá medirse a Luka Doncic. El base reconoció que tiene marcada esa cita en el calendario y que le gustaría enfrentarse al esloveno tanto en defensa como en ataque. "Sobre todo sí que me gustaría jugar contra Luka, defenderlo, atacarlo. La verdad es que es a día de hoy mi equis en el calendario", confesó. La elección tiene un componente especial: De Larrea explicó que se siente identificado con los Mavericks y con su organización, de la que ha sido seguidor durante años. También se mostró optimista con las opciones del equipo esta temporada y, cuando le preguntaron quién ganaría el anillo, no dudó: Dallas.

articles.title: Explaining the NBA Rule Changes for 2026-27 Season, Including NBA Cup Bracket Format
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NBA season, which tips off Tuesday night, brings a host of new things to the hoops world.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season, which tips off Tuesday night, brings a host of new things to the hoops world.

There is a fresh, ballyhooed batch of rookies, a flock of familiar faces in new places and a new set of challenges to traverse this 82-game gauntlet.

On that latter point, there are some tweaks to the way the league will handle the draft lottery, the Emirates NBA Cup and certain on-court calls, so let's examine and explain these changes.

Tired of the unsightly (but, under the old system, often understandable) act of tanking, the NBA's Board of Governors overhauled the draft lottery system to directly combat it. The new 3-2-1 Lottery system takes effect this season and will be in place for the 2027, 2028 and 2029 drafts.

It's a pretty dramatic departure from the norm, which explains why it was only approved for essentially a three-year trial run. It should lessen the most egregious forms of tanking, although it could also wind up punishing a few misfortunate franchises just for lacking talent.

As for the changes , there might be too many to mention, but some of the biggest are flattened lottery odds, an expansion from 14 to 16 teams, a drawing for all 16 lottery picks and restrictions from picking first in consecutive drafts or owning top-five picks in three consecutive drafts. There's also a draft relegation for the teams with the worst three records, who will hold worse odds of a top-nine pick than the other non-play-in teams.

For those who felt the league had to do something to address tanking, it certainly took a big swing and attempted to do a whole lot. No one knows how it will look in practice, but it should change the way bottom-feeders approach the final stretch run.

New (and Historic) Setting for Emirates NBA Cup

The tournament, now in its fourth year, will no longer hold its semifinal and championship games at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. Now, the higher-seeded team in each conference will host the semifinals, and the two teams to advance will face each other in a championship game at historic Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, the home of Butler University.

As for the tournament itself, Group Play runs from Friday, Oct. 30 through Friday, Nov. 27. The Knockout Rounds start on Friday, Dec. 4, and the championship will be played on Friday, Dec. 11. All games of the tournament count toward the regular-season standings, other than the finale.

The first three NBA Cups crowned three different champions. The Los Angeles Lakers won the inaugural event, the Milwaukee Bucks won the second and the New York Knicks won the most recent.

While the NBA doesn't rule out changes every year, it will often have certain areas of focus for its officials.

Now, these things are sometimes stressed early in the season and not so much later on, but that can happen because the action involved is effectively taken out of the game (like transition take fouls, for instance).

For the 2026-27 season, the league is lasering in on push-offs . Referees are now gauging feeling, firming, force and full extension. In short, ball-handlers can use their off arms to feel for their defender or firm up in front of them, but they cannot contact defenders with force or create advantages with full arm extensions.

Refs are also instructed to watch illegal screens, along with illegal defensive contact that impedes movement, like clutching and grabbing off the ball. There's also an emphasis on "straight-line pathway plays," where offensive or defensive players can be called for a foul for going out of their way to bump the other off of their direct path toward the basket.

South Carolina was the overwhelming pick in the preseason Associated Press Top 25 poll in women's basketball.

The Gamecocks received 23 first-place votes compared to six for No. 2 UConn.

South Carolina coach Dawn Staley called the No. 1 ranking "a gift and curse."

"I tend to not look at the number, but our players do," she told the AP's Doug Feinberg . "They look at it and feel like there's a sense of respect to being No. 1. They also know that it's pressure packed with the type of non-conference schedule we have, we're going to be challenged. If we stand there at No. 1 at the end of our non-conference season that's something to be truly to be proud of."

The Gamecocks lost Madina Okot, Ta'Niya Latson and Raven Johnson to the WNBA, but they retained leading scorer Joyce Edwards. Tessa Johnson is back as well after averaging 12.8 points and shooting 44.8 percent from beyond the arc.

In terms of additions, Staley signed a quartet of 5-star recruits: Kelsi Andrews, Oliviyah Edwards, Jerzy Robinson and Kaeli Wynn. Guards Brooke Quarles-Daniels and Jordan Lee should make an immediate impact out of the transfer portal as well.

A Nov. 24 meeting between South Carolina and UConn is bound to determine which of the two is the early national title favorite.

Huskies forward Sarah Strong is the best player in the country. She averaged 18.4 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.4 steals and 1.6 blocks en route to winning the Wade Trophy.

Azzi Fudd is a big loss for coach Geno Auriemma, but Blanca Quiñonez, Ashlynn Shade and KK Arnold will all help to provide some continuity.

Reigning national champion UCLA is a total wild card after an offseason exodus.

The Bruins' No. 11 ranking is a sign that coach Cori Close and her staff brought in some reinforcements, but overcoming the exits of Lauren Betts, Kiki Rice, Gabriela Jaquez, Gianna Kneepkens, Angela Dugalić and Charlisse Leger-Walker is a tall order.

Crosstown rival USC is a bit of an unknown for much different reasons.

Star guard JuJu Watkins was sidelined for all of last season as she recovered from a torn ACL in the 2025 NCAA tournament. Her absence allowed Jazzy Davidson to shine as the true freshman averaged 17.9 points and 4.1 assists.

The Trojans could have the most explosive backcourt in the country, but Watkins is coming off a major injury and will have to adjust to a new role. She maintained a 37.9 percent usage rate through her first two years, per Sports Reference , and that number will have to come down in order for Davison to build on what she achieved in 2025-26.

The Trojans won't have to wait long to be tested in a big way as they head to Greenville, South Carolina, to play the Gamecocks on Nov. 15.

articles.title: Wild coach John Hynes reveals how much longer Filip Gustavsson will be out
articles.summary: The Minnesota Wild are off to a terrific start in 2026-27, going 6-2-1 and sitting in second place in the Central Division. Jesper Wallstedt has been a cata...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Wild are off to a terrific start in 2026-27, going 6-2-1 and sitting in second place in the Central Division. Jesper Wallstedt has been a catalyst, starting eight of nine games and posting a sparkling 1.99 goals-against average and .922 save percentage.

The 23-year-old is the goalie of the future in Saint Paul, although he should form one of the NHL's better tandems alongside Filip Gustavsson when his countryman returns.

Gustavsson continues to recover from offseason hip surgery , and head coach John Hynes told reporters Sunday, including Jess Myers of the Pioneer Press, that the netminder remains at least another month away .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Quite a ways," Hynes said when asked how far away a potential return might be.

Gustavsson has begun skating on his own, providing an encouraging step in his recovery, but he has yet to rejoin team practices.

Wild general manager Bill Guerin signed Calvin Pickard over the summer as insurance. The veteran backup allowed five goals on 25 shots in his lone start of the campaign, a 5-2 defeat against the Winnipeg Jets on Oct. 13.

"I thought he battled hard. He made some big saves for us," Hynes said of Pickard's performance. "He hadn't played in a while, so I thought he looked sharp. He came in, and I felt like we could have been a little bit better in front of him in the second and third period."

Gustavsson signed a five-year, $34 million contract extension with Minnesota last year before going 28-15-6 in 2025-26. His struggles late in the regular season opened the door for Wallstedt, who ended up playing 10 of the team's 11 games in the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs.

The 28-year-old remains a capable No. 1 option, although Wallstedt appears to have taken the lead in Minnesota's crease. His excellent start this season has only strengthened that position.

Wallstedt will become a restricted free agent with arbitration rights next summer and could command a significant raise from his current $2.2 million average annual value.

When Gustavsson is ready to return, Guerin will have a decision to make. Pickard could be waived or traded, although keeping three goaltenders on the roster remains an option.

For now, Minnesota will continue leaning heavily on Wallstedt as it waits to reunite a tandem capable of helping the Wild compete for a Stanley Cup in 2027.

articles.title: Why is the NBA trying unusual start to its season?
articles.summary: The NBA's regular season is starting at 3:00 PM ET. Why are they trying this?
articles.body:
The NBA is making history as it starts the 2026-2027 season. For the first time ever, the league will open its regular season with a triple-header.

NBA action starting at 3:00 PM ET? That's exactly what we get when the Boston Celtics visit the Detroit Pistons . The New York Knicks raise their championship banner at 7:00 PM ET as LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers are in the house. The nightcap is one of the NBA's best rivalries. The Oklahoma City Thunder take on the San Antonio Spurs at 9:30 PM ET. NBC/Peacock will broadcast all games nationally.

So why is the NBA trying something different this year?

Why is the first NBA regular season game at 3:00 PM ET?

NBA fans expect a standard double-header to start the regular season. You would probably get LeBron James, the defending champ, and maybe a young superstar-led squad. Now we're getting three games starting in the afternoon.

They're doing this just to be different. Professional sports leagues have to innovate, and this is one way Adam Silver is trying. Everyone is roasting the in-season tournament, and it ended up being pretty high-level basketball.

There isn't a day without MLB playoff games right now, and it's not an NFL game day either. There's no competition other than the NHL . These games feature big markets and mostly marketable superstars, so they could catch the attention of casual fans. They might choose to watch Jayson Tatum instead of a standard soap opera on TV.

The National Basketball Association is truly an international game now. International players have won eight straight NBA MVPs. People worldwide love watching the NBA and its biggest stars.

Games throughout the day let people in different time zones catch them in the morning or during the day. Some viewers around the world won't have to watch at crazy times in the middle of the night.

articles.body:
This story, by staff writer Sean Deveney first appeared in the May 26, 2003, issue of The Sporting News under the headline "Ready for prime time | LeBron James will be taken first in the draft, his team determined in a lottery shifted to nighttime to capitalize on his popularity, but his No. 1 status likely has as much to do with ticket sales as talent."

Welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to this installment of The Drafting Game, the annual reality program that finds the most eligible basketball bachelors in the country—or, world—and matches them with the hopeful dregs of American professional basketball. Three (very) young men have been selected among hundreds of hopefuls, and soon a contestant will be chosen to pick among these three. That contestant will be carefully selected through a well-monitored and entirely honest system (we would never, ever accuse anyone of rigging The Drafting Game, of course). Now, ladies and gentlemen, let's meet the bachelors!

Words and excitement are not terms usually associated with the NBA draft lottery—try "mandate" and "nap-worthy"—but, without question, 2003 will be different. This year, there is hoopla. There is hullabaloo. Usually, the lottery is awkwardly wedged into the halftime show of a Sunday afternoon playoff broadcast, but this year it has been stretched into a half-hour, prime-time show, a drama (working title: The Elgin Baylor Chronicles) that ABC will put up against Thursday night staples Friends and CSI.

There's only one reason this lottery has landed in prime time: It's the LeBron-a-thon, and the TV network is Exhibit A in the case for Akron prep star LeBron James as the No. 1 pick in the draft. The sports-loving nation is so intrigued by his potential that ABC thinks it can knock off the small-screen heavyweights with 30 minutes of David Stern opening envelopes. Such is the hype and delusion around James that there is not much chance of there being any rational thinking when it comes to making the first pick.

"Imagine the team with the top pick taking someone other than James. It can't happen. James has played in three high school all-star games and sold out all three. Where the EA Sports Roundball Classic drew 5,712 fans to Northwestern University in Evanston, Ill., two years ago, it drew 19,678 at Chicago's United Center in March. That's the power of James."

"Who knows how good he is?" says Michael Lynn, the managing editor of Team Marketing Report. "But it doesn't matter. It's impossible to put a number on his impact until after you draft him, but whoever has him is going to sell season-ticket packages. They're going to sell out games. They're going to sell parking, concessions, shirts, hats, merchandise, everything. You will sell all that before the season starts. If he is any good, it will just mushroom from there. It will be close to Michael Jordan coming back for Washington."

Thus, the possibility of a kit-shake for picks 1a and 1b—in particular order: Syracuse freshman Carmelo Anthony and Yugoslavian forward Darko Milicic—is out the window. There is too much money to be made from James. Both Anthony and Darko deserve better. James may be the clear No. 1, but what is not clear is whether that choice is based on athletic potential or marketing potential. "You'd have to work out all three, at least, to compare them," one college coach said. "And my best guess would be that it would be close, but James might not come out on top."

Thus, we at TSN have got together The Drafting Game—plan evaluations of the top three prospects, untrammeled by economics, line of hype and assembled with the belief that the draft should not be a popularity contest.

He says he is a sucker for old-fashioned things (especially sports jerseys) and even owns his own SUV—though he points out that he is much better at driving the lane than driving near parked cars. His hobbies include a headband collection, participating in lively debates on shoe contracts and referring to himself in the third person. Fellas, let's meet LeBron!

Is it all SUVs and headbands with James, or will he make his mark with substance and sweat? We'll see.

"You have to remember that he was one of the top high school football prospects in the country as a wide receiver last year," says draft expert Chris Monroe of Akron Draft News. "He is a great athlete. He can play point guard, shooting guard or small forward, and it's that versatility that makes him the No. 1 pick."

LeBron says: "My last year in high school, we played the best teams in the country. I played 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7–10 players all my senior year. I'd play my game and just keep the work ethic that I have. I'll be successful at the next level."

Best-case scenario: Magic Johnson meets Tracy McGrady; worst-case scenario: Derrick Coleman meets Ricky Davis.

The skinny: At this point, James has more ability than any prep player who previously has made the jump to the NBA, with the possible exception of Kevin Garnett. Even at 6-8, 240 pounds, James can handle the ball, cross up defenders and blow by them with his unpredictable first step. He is a first-rate passer with a knack for the cutting, and he scores with McGrady and Kobe Bryant as the country's best finishers at the rim.

Two aspects of James' game that most often are questioned are his shooting and his defense. But playing against high school competition, he rarely had to defend a player with comparable skills, so his defense is an unknown, not a negative. He has the physical tools to become a very good defender, just as Garnett, Bryant and McGrady have. His shot is streakier, and because of that, he probably will struggle early in his career. He must work on it.

That's the other unknown about James: his willingness to work. It's going to take many practice court sessions to improve his game. Never has there been as pampered a top pick in the league, and whether James finds time in his off-court schedule to improve as a player remains to be seen. But it's work that separates a guy such as Bryant from a guy such as Davis.

He was a big man on campus last year, and though he is laid-back, he certainly is not "Melo" when it comes to big-time performances. He promises he would never stand you up, unless it was in the past. If he were to give you a gift, it would be a ring—just don't ask for that big gold one he got from the NCAA. Now, let's meet Carmelo!

Carmelo says: "Of course I would take me No. 1. What kind of player would I be if I didn't?"

Best-case scenario: Chris Webber on the wing, only without the baggage; worst-case scenario: A skinnier Glenn Robinson.

The skinny: They call him Mello, and not just because of his first name—Carmelo Anthony really is a laid-back guy. So laid-back, in fact, that some scouts weren't sure he had the fire to succeed at the next level. "Then came the tournament," one front-office executive says. "He made a lot of people into believers."

With the 6-8, 220-pound Anthony leading Syracuse's run to the NCAA championship in April, whisperers around the NBA premiere that he could, perhaps, displace James as the league's top pick. He earned more recognition but also earned a reputation as a player who had guts and chutzpah. Teams can only hope Milicic and James have those qualities. The No. 1 chatter has faded, though Anthony is not sure why.

"To me, I had the chance to play on the big stage," Anthony says. "Everybody saw us. And we won."

The biggest disadvantage Anthony has is that he is a pure small forward, not possessing the versatility and explosive burst that James has.

and not wide enough to be a low-post banger. Darko what? Look around the league, and there are few 6-foot-8 small forwards, players who have the size, athleticism and shooting range to play 15 to 20 feet from the hoop, combined with the savvy to operate in the post when mismatches come. Players who have those abilities—Antoine Walker or Tim Duncan, for example—often misuse them.

Anthony can hit the midrange jumper much better than James. He is an underrated passer and could one day play a point forward role, the way Jamal Mashburn or Scottie Pippen did. Like James, his defense should be called an unknown, not a negative, because Syracuse played a 2-3 zone.

And don't forget that when Anthony was in high school two years ago at Oak Hill Academy, he put 34 points on James and the St. Vincent-St. Mary squad. "I remember that like it was yesterday," Anthony says. "I usually remember that: we won, though."

Now, folks, Bachelor No. 3 is tall, Darko and handsome but does not say much—in English, at least—which only adds to his status as an international man of mystery. His hobbies include eating cevapcici (don't worry, it's just sausage), putting on weight and correcting people who mispronounce his last name. Let's hear it for Darko!

Darko says: "I have not seen LeBron James play, but he is playing against kids his age or younger. I am going against 30-year-old men every day."

Best-case scenario: Toni Kukoc meets Kevin Garnett; worst-case scenario: Shawn Bradley meets Nikoloz Tskitishvili.

The skinny: Take everything you think you know about European big men—a little awkward, soft defensively, slow—and throw it out. That's not Milicic.

"He's the real deal," says former Ohio State center Slobodan Savic, now playing for Crvena Zvezda in Yugoslavia. "I have seen LeBron, and I have played against Darko. It's a tough call, but Darko is a legit 7-footer who can shoot, handle, pass, and he is only 17. It's hard to describe the kid to you unless you see him."

Savic isn't alone in his praise. One NBA GM, speaking off the record, said comparing James with Milicic, who measures 7-0, 250 pounds: "Milicic is not going to sell tickets, no matter how good he is. But as Detroit president Joe Dumars says, 'If we draft Darko and put him into an American high school for a whole season, it would be ridiculous. It would be a joke. That is how good he is.'"

Still, Milicic may be the best player in the draft. He is not the athlete James and Anthony are, but he is a good shooter whose game is more suited to the NBA than to the European league. He would be lethal in NBA pick-and-rolls, and he is athletic enough to create off of isolations, which are not common in European basketball. He also can run the floor and finish fast breaks.

Milicic has the inclination to play tough interior defense, but he does not yet have the body. He can be pushed off the block, though he often manages to get a hand on shots. He has to work on some fundamentals, like holding the ball high after rebounds to keep from being stripped by stronger players. He'll need work, but the finished product could be every bit as good as James, only in a 7-foot frame.

Milicic might be the most skilled player in the draft and is athletic enough to get his own shot.

There you have it, folks—LeBron and these two other guys, our beloved bachelors. Now, all we need to do is select our contestants. Be sure to tune in Thursday for the stunning conclusion of ... The Drafting Game!

articles.title: Celtics game could tip off while you're at work. Why it starts at 3 p.m.
articles.summary: Today's Celtics season opener against the Detroit Pistons starts early in the afternoon. Here's why.
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics ' first game of the 2026-2027 regular season is Tuesday, Oct. 20, against the Detroit Pistons .

Boston will tip off its season with a midday matchup at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit. The team is entering its first season after star player Jaylen Brown was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers .

The Celtics are coming off a 125-120 win over Brown and the 76ers in Philadelphia on Friday in their final preseason game.

The Celtics-Pistons game is the earliest of three games on the NBA's opening day schedule Tuesday, followed by the Philadelphia 76ers vs. New York Knicks and Oklahoma City Thunder vs. San Antonio Spurs . The Knicks are expected to raise their championship banner and receive their rings before taking the court.

According to the injury report ahead of Tuesday's Celtics game, guard Devin Carter (#22) is out due to an illness.

Here's what to know about today's Celtics game, including why it tips off so early in the day.

What time does Celtics vs. Pistons game start?

The Celtics vs. Pistons game is set to tip off at 3 p.m. ET, according to the NBA schedule .

Fans can watch the Celtics vs. Pistons on NBC. They can also stream it on Peacock or Fubo .

How to listen to Celtics game on the radio

You can listen to the Celtics game on on 98.5 FM The Sports Hub , the flagship station of the Boston team, according to its website. You can also listen on Sirius XM .

If you live in Providence, you can listen to coverage of the game on WPRV 790 AM.

Why does the Celtics game start so early in the day?

The Celtics game starts early in the afternoon to accommodate three in NBA games on opening day: Celtics vs. Pistons at 3 p.m. ET, Philadelphia 76ers vs. New York Knicks at 7 p.m. ET, and Oklahoma City Thunder vs. San Antonio Spurs at 9:30 p.m. ET.

It'll be the first time in 15 years that more than two games will be played on the first day of the NBA season, and the first-ever NBA opening-day tripleheader broadcast nationally.

It's an experiment conceived by the NBA and NBC entering Year 2 of their massive 11-year, $27-billion media rights partnership , with the goal of turning opening night into an all-day event.

NBC saw an opportunity to generate excitement ahead of the two primetime windows that have typically defined the NBA's regular season debut. The network pointed to strong viewership for its 2026 Major League Baseball Opening Day doubleheader, which also began with an afternoon game.

Mark Giannotto of USA TODAY contributed to this report.
