articles.title: AJ Dybantsa ruled out by Wizards for season opener vs. Bucks due to ankle injury
articles.summary: The 2026 No. 1 overall draft pick left Friday's preseason finale after awkwardly landing on his left ankle.
articles.body:
AJ Dybantsa's NBA debut will have to wait until at least Friday.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft will sit out Wednesday's season opener for the Washington Wizards with a sprained ankle . Dybantsa suffered the injury during last Friday's preseason finale against the New Orleans Pelicans.

Wizards head coach Brian Keefe told reporters that Dybantsa is considered day-to-day.

Dybantsa left the game against the Pelicans last week after landing awkwardly on his left ankle following a shot. He limped to the locker room for further evaluation and did not return. Keefe said the decision to keep him out for the rest of the game was a precautionary measure.

A positive sign for Dybantsa is that he took part in shooting drills on Monday and was seen during Tuesday's practice.

Following Wednesday's game against the Milwaukee Bucks, the Wizards will remain at home on Friday when they welcome the Toronto Raptors.

articles.title: LeBron James' Use of Fanatics Helicopter Addressed by Adam Silver Ahead of 76ers Debut
articles.summary: NBA commissioner Adam Silver doesn't believe LeBron James' means of transportation for his commute to Philadelphia merits any further scrutiny from the league for the time being.
articles.body:
NBA commissioner Adam Silver doesn't believe LeBron James' means of transportation for his commute to Philadelphia merits any further scrutiny from the league for the time being.

Appearing Tuesday on The Pat McAfee Show , Silver said that "there's no rules issue there whatsoever" as long as James struck a deal with Fanatics independent of any involvement from the Philadelphia 76ers.

Front Office Sports' Daniel Roberts and TMZ Sports reported earlier this month Fanatics is footing the bill for LeBron's trips as part of his endorsement deal with the company.

Fanatics founder Michael Rubin used to own a share of the Sixers but sold it in 2022.

Investigative reporter Pablo Torre, who was the first to lift the lid on the salary cap circumvention by the Los Angeles Clippers and Kawhi Leonard, told Roberts earlier this month that some NBA owners reached out to him to discuss James' unique situation:

The partnership between James and Fanatics far predates his move to Philadelphia. The 22-time All-Star signed an exclusive trading card deal with the company in 2024.

In terms of the helicopter specifically, Roberts noted that "a small handful of other athletes with big Fanatics deals get same access."

On the heels of the Clippers/Aspiration scandal and given Rubin's past ties to the Sixers, the questions over James' transportation setup are understandable. Everything nonetheless appears to be pretty straightforward and aboveboard.

articles.title: Adam Silver Updates NBA Expansion Timeline Amid Las Vegas, Seattle, Mexico City Buzz
articles.summary: NBA commissioner Adam Silver provided a timeline and update on league expansion during Tuesday's edition of the Pat McAfee Show (25-second mark).
articles.body:
NBA commissioner Adam Silver provided a timeline and update on league expansion during Tuesday's edition of the Pat McAfee Show (25-second mark).

"We're still a few seasons away from actual expansion taking place, but as you said, we've been public about the fact that we're looking closely at Las Vegas and Seattle," Silver said.

"Las Vegas seems to have an insatiable appetite for sports and entertainment. Several groups now are thinking of even building a brand-new arena in town, which at least the presentation is maybe the most spectacular arena ever.

"Seattle has a great arena, there's a great NBA tradition there, so we're looking closely at returning to Seattle.

"I've mentioned maybe down the road, there's Mexico City, largest city in North America, burgeoning a huge basketball base. Fans in Mexico, large Mexican-American population. So a bunch of different opportunities out there, and discussions are ongoing about Las Vegas and Seattle right now."

According to Mick Akers of the Las Vegas Review-Journal , there is a leading group for a Las Vegas team:

"The bid group including Nancy Walton Laurie her husband, Bill Laurie, and Silver Lake co-CEO and Raiders minority owner Egon Durban, who recently joined the group, is the heavy favorite to land Las Vegas' NBA team, a person with knowledge of the situation told the Review-Journal . The source is not authorized to comment on the situation."

It seems to be a matter of when—not if—Vegas will get a team. Over the past decade, Vegas has added four pro sports teams in the Aces, Golden Knights and Raiders. The Athletics are on the way soon, and an as-of-now unnamed PWHL team is as well.

There seems to be some murkiness regarding Seattle, although the city has been talked about ad nauseam as an expansion destination and a place for the NBA to return since the SuperSonics left for Oklahoma City in 2008. Seattle has a passionate sports fanbase that absolutely deserves an NBA team.

According to ESPN's Brian Windhorst , "NBA commissioner Adam Silver appears to be upping the ante on the leverage game involving the possible future of the Seattle SuperSonics, multiple ownership sources told ESPN.

"We say 'possible' with care because Silver left owners with the impression that a Seattle expansion team was no longer a lock at last month's board of governors meeting. Silver even reintroduced the idea of Mexico City as a possible destination.

"At the meeting, owners were told about at least one Mexico City-based group that has approached NBA expansion partner PJT Partners with a plan about launching a team and developing a new arena district there that apparently has caught the league's attention, several sources said."

Windhorst added that the league is "full-go" on expanding to Las Vegas and the league "does not seem happy" with bids from groups who want to bring a team to Seattle. Time could change that, though.

Mexico City has a population of just over 9.2 million (with a metro area of 21.8 million), so that could be an intriguing option. The NBA has previously placed a G League team there (Mexico City Capitanes), and the league is set to host a game on Nov. 7 when the Denver Nuggets and Indiana Pacers play.

Ultimately, NBA expansion would take a few years to actually come to fruition, but it's on the horizon. This would mark the first time the league expanded since the Charlotte Bobcats joined the league in 2004.

articles.title: RJ Luis Reportedly Won't Be Eligible for LSU, Would Have Violated Rules After Signing NBA Contract
articles.summary: Former St. John's star RJ Luis won't get to play for LSU this season after all.
articles.body:
Former St. John's star RJ Luis won't get to play for LSU this season after all.

Per CBS Sports' Matt Norlander , Luis will not be cleared by the SEC to suit up for the Tigers in 2026-27 because he would be in violation of the conference's rule that prevents players from returning to college after signing a pro contract. Luis went undrafted in 2025 and signed a two-way contract before later signing an Exhibit 10 contract with the Boston Celtics' G League affiliate in Maine.

Luis signed with LSU in May and filed a lawsuit against the NCAA, which granted a preliminary injunction that declared him eligible for the 2026-27 season. The day after receiving his injunction, the SEC announced its new rules to prevent professional athletes from returning to college teams.

Still, Norlander noted that LSU head coach Will Wade "had been privately confident for months" that Luis would eventually be deemed eligible to play, but the SEC "would not budge." Sources told Norlander that in recent days, Wade "has come to accept the reality that Luis would not be allowed to compete for LSU this season."

The 2025 Big East Player of the Year in his final season with St. John's, Luis was a promising prospect with averages of 18.2 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.0 assists. He was named Most Outstanding Player of the Big East Tournament after leading the Red Storm to a conference championship.

ESPN's Myron Metcalf reported that LSU was picked to finish 14th out of 16 teams in the SEC preseason poll, so the Tigers could use all the help they can get. However, they will have to forge ahead without Luis when they open the 2026-27 campaign on Nov. 3 against LSU New Orleans.

articles.title: 100 bold NBA predictions for 2026-27, forecasting every team's season
articles.summary: Here are 100 predictions ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
Here are 100 predictions ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season:

1. Atlanta wins 41 games (43.5 over/under) and makes the play-in tournament.

2. Hawks fans clamor for Kingston Flemings to get more minutes . Flemings had 21 assists to only five turnovers during the preseason. It's just preseason, yeah. But the rookie top-10 pick looked like a reliable facilitator and his speedy drives will lead to some big highlights coming off the bench to begin the year.

3. Jalen Johnson makes an All-NBA team again. Expect another leap from him this year as a scorer.

4. Dyson Daniels shoots below 20% from 3 again . He made only 18.8% on 1.5 attempts per game last year. He was jacking them up in preseason, but continued to struggle to make shots and his mechanics look no better.

5. Boston wins 56 games (51.5 over/under), grabs the top seed in the East and makes the East finals.

6. Hugo González takes a big leap as a scorer. He already established himself as an elite hustle guy last season. During the summer playing with Spain and this preseason, he's looked far more dynamic and comfortable with the ball in his hands.

7. Jayson Tatum finishes top five in MVP voting. From the 2022-23 season through 2024-25, Tatum averaged 31.5 points, 8.3 boards, and 5.4 assists per 75 possessions with only a minor decline in scoring efficiency.

8. Brooklyn wins 25 games, hitting the over (24.5 over/under).

9. Nets fans get disgusted with Julius Randle. He might lead to a few more wins over the course of the season, but ultimately his ball-stopping, mopiness and mere presence will take away opportunities from some of the more impressive young players that offer hope for a brighter future.

10. Mikel Brown has multiple 40-point games. The rookie guard can catch fire at any given moment, and with his skill set he's not overly reliant on just the jumper or just at-rim finishing. He can do everything. Nets fans are going to fall in love.

11. Charlotte wins 36 games (39.5 over/under) and misses the playoffs. The East is just so deep and loaded. Someone good will need to underwhelm, and already the Hornets are impacted by key injuries to Kon Knueppel and Coby White.

12. The Hornets lead the NBA in 3-point rate. Despite trading LaMelo Ball, Charlotte still has a roster full of shooters. The Hornets were first in makes but second in rate last year. It was Golden State who was first. Based on preseason play, the Warriors could be taking a step back, moving Charlotte into the first slot.

13. Chicago wins 27 games (29.5 over/under) and misses the playoffs.

14. The Bulls trade Norm Powell. Even though Powell is one of the only knockdown shooters on the team, at 34, he'll be in high demand come trade deadline time.

15. Bulls fans will question whether the core has enough shooting. As high as I am on all three of Caleb Wilson, Matas Buzelis and Josh Giddey, I do think there's a legitimate question whether the three of them offer enough shooting (very similar to the Orlando Magic with Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero).

16. Cleveland wins 44 games (47.5 over/under) and makes the playoffs through the play-in tournament.

17. Evan Mobley plateaus on offense. For all his media day talk about improving his offensive game, he didn't look all too different during preseason. His handle is still clunky, his shot is still average. There's little reason to believe he's going to become the creator that the Cavaliers need.

18. Cavs fans will question the Peyton Watson move. Watson is a solid role player. But he really only had a single 15-game stretch of his career in which he looked like he warrants the contract he received. Other than that? He was a solid role player. Not much more.

19. Jaylon Tyson has a big year off the bench, shoots over 40% from 3, and posts over three assists per game.

20. Dallas wins 41 games (34.5 over/under) and makes the playoffs through the play-in tournament.

21. Cooper Flagg makes an All-NBA team, averaging 27.8 points, 7.5 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game.

22. Flagg and Kyrie Irving are both named All-Stars. And if a Comeback Player of the Year Award existed, Irving would win it.

23. Denver wins 51 games (49.5 over/under) and grabs the third seed in the West.

24. Aaron Gordon is named an All-Star for the first time in his career.

25. Denver's depth is its Achilles' heel. The backup bigs don't provide enough support behind Nikola Jokić. DeMar DeRozan puts up points but not much else. A trade will need to be made.

26. Detroit wins 51 games (49.5 over/under). After winning 60 games last year and then improving the roster this summer, it's a bit strange that the Pistons are projected for under 50 wins — and that's coming from me, a Pistons skeptic!

27. Trajan Langdon makes a trade. The Pistons still need more shooting. He'll cash in some chips to find it on the market.

28. Ron Holland falls out of the rotation. The Pistons have way more options now, and they need more spacers not defenders. He likely ends up on the trade block as a result.

29. Jalen Duren starts taking 3s. Whether it'll be for better or worse is harder to predict, but I'm taking him for his word that "it's time" to start shooting them after he started taking midrange pull-ups last year.

30. Golden State wins 28 games (37.5 over/under), hitting the under by the widest margin of any team in the NBA. This is fueled by an injury-riddled year to their core pieces with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody already sidelined, and Kristaps Porziņģis dealing with his situation.

31. Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler get traded, and Warriors fans end up happier that the franchise has finally chosen a direction. Stephen Curry will still be there, but now he'll be surrounded by impressive young players.

32. Yaxel Lendeborg finishes in the top three for Rookie of the Year voting.

33. Houston wins 47 games (48.5 over/under).

34. The team shoots way more 3s. The Rockets were 19th in 3-pointers per game last season. That'll rise into the top-7 this season.

35. Rockets fans question Alperen Şengün's upside. It's been a long time hoping that Şengün will start making jumpers, an important development for him given the lower volume shooters elsewhere on the roster. Things didn't look all too improved this preseason.

36. Indiana wins 45 games (43.5 over/under).

37. Tyrese Haliburton makes an All-NBA team and looks exactly like the superstar who we last saw in 2024-25.

38. Ivica Zubac proves to be the best center Haliburton has ever played with. Despite not shooting 3s, he does everything else imaginable better than Haliburton's old partner, Myles Turner.

39. Los Angeles wins 22 games (28.5 over/under).

40. The Clippers become trade deadline sellers. Collectively, the Clippers don't have a good roster. But individually, there are pieces that could appeal to plenty of contenders: Derrick Jones, Brook Lopez, Rui Hachimura, Kris Dunn, Max Strus and Brandon Ingram. Expect the Clippers to trade some of them.

41. Keaton Wagler makes an All-Rookie team, and he and Yanic Konan Niederhäuser look like the pick-and-roll combo of the future.

42. Los Angeles wins 47 games (46.5 over/under).

43. Luka Dončić has the best season of his career. Think about what Luka did after the deadline last year prior to his injury. Now apply that to this season with him in even better shape and a better fitting supporting cast. Luka will get MVP votes, and even win it if Wemby doesn't hit 65 games.

44. Collin Sexton receives Sixth Man votes. I've been waiting since Sexton was in college to see him playing in a winning basketball environment. Finally, he's going to get that chance and it's going to lead to a lot of recognition he's never received before.

45. The Lakers defense is terrible without Walker Kessler. I have little doubt that Kessler will be an excellent defensive anchor when he's on the floor. But there are serious concerns about what the team looks like without him. The Lakers will need to find a better backup center via trade.

46. Memphis wins 38 games (29.5 over/under), hitting the over by the widest margin of any team in the NBA.

47. Cam Boozer wins Rookie of the Year and even draws All-Star replacement consideration.

48. Cedric Coward shoots over 40% from 3 after shooting just 34% as a rookie.

49. Miami wins 49 games (46.5 over/under).

50. Giannis Antetokounmpo posts a career high in assists. It looked like we witnessed Point Giannis out there this preseason. The Heat shot an unsustainable percentage on his passes, but it still looks like he's shaping up to exceed seven assists per game for the first time in his career.

51. The Heat will need more shot creation. As nice as Davion Mitchell and Ryan Conwell are, this season will end with Heat fans feeling like the team needs to improve at guard — whether that comes internally from one of them or externally with a trade.

52. The Bucks win 26 games (25.5 over/under).

54. Bucks fans are ecstatic by year's end. Taylor Jenkins is a great development coach, and this team is loaded with talented young players. Whether it's the guys received in return for Giannis (I am especially interested to see what Kasparas Jakučionis and Kel'el Ware can do) or the rookies (Brayden Burries might be the real deal), there's lots to like about what's brewing in Milwaukee.

55. Minnesota wins 49 games (48.5 over/under).

56. Anthony Edwards makes a career-high amount of 3s per game. With LaMelo Ball on the roster, more of those will come off the catch than ever before.

57. Minnesota's defense will be better than ever in the Rudy Gobert era. Why? No more Julius Randle and Naz Reid. Way more Joan Beringer off the bench, and a ton of guards and wings who play with grit. The Gobert minutes will always dominate defensively, but now he has support behind him.

58. Zyon Pullin will end up earning minutes. A deep cut here on a two-way guard, but Pullin looked like the better fitting backup guard over Bones Hyland in preseason. It wouldn't be a shocker if that pans out true during the year too.

59. New Orleans wins 26 games (28.5 over/under), the same amount as last season. It's not that the team will be worse, it's just that the rest of the league is so much better now.

60. Jeremiah Fears resembles a future star, but Derik Queen continues to underwhelm.

61. Joe Dumars resists more trade offers for Trey Murphy, even though he should probably take them.

62. New York wins 51 games (52.5 over/under) with an up-and-down regular season that very much resembles last year ahead of the championship run.

63. The Knicks do not repeat as champions.

64. Mitchell Robinson is not missed on the court. The collective of Andre Drummond, Mo Diawara, and even James Wiseman, fill backup frontcourt minutes admirably.

65. Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart are re-signed , and the Knicks avoid the second apron. That means bye-bye to Deuce McBride.

66. The Thunder win 62 games, the most in the NBA (62.5 over/under) and go on to win their second NBA Finals in three seasons.

67. Ajay Mitchell wins Sixth Man of the Year.

68. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander makes a career-high in 3s per game as he takes a career-high amount of off-ball 3s.

69. Aday Mara is named first-team All-Rookie.

70. OKC's decision to trade Lu Dort and Isaiah Joe proves to be beneficial to the team since more players who can generate shots off the dribble receive minutes: Cason Wallace, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Bennett Stirtz, Nikola Topić, and Aday Mara all receive opportunities that make the Thunder overall more dynamic.

71. Orlando wins 41 games (43.5 over/under).

72. Sean Sweeney impresses as head coach. It doesn't necessarily show up in the wins column because of how loaded the East is this year. But the Sweeney system will bring out the best of Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner.

73. But the Magic still need more shooting. Next summer, Orlando will need to add more shooters to make this team really shine.

74. Philadelphia wins 52 games (50.5 over/under) and makes the East finals.

75. The Sixers don't win the NBA Finals, and the durability of Joel Embiid is the main reason why. I love Embiid, so it pains me to say that. But he looks like a shell of his former self, and the Sixers don't have much big man support behind him.

76. Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe continue trending way up. As much as this year is about winning a title with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown (and a bunch of veteran role players) now on the team, it's also about watching the kids get better. And they will. Maxey is only 25 and could have a career-year playing off LeBron, and Edgecombe will continue flashing two-way star upside.

77. Phoenix wins 41 games (40.5 over/under) and misses the playoffs through the play-in tournament.

78. Devin Booker continues to underwhelm. Booker's 3-point shooting and at-rim finishing has dipped ever since Chris Paul departed Phoenix. Those concerns continued this preseason with him making only two of his 16 shots from 3.

79. Khaman Maluach takes the starting center job. As much as I like Oso Ighodaro, Maluach provides higher upside as a center who can both protect the rim and space the floor.

80. Portland wins 41 games (41.5 over/under) and makes the playoffs through the play-in tournament.

81. Too many guards prove to be an issue. Damian Lillard and Ja Morant are both making comebacks. Scoot Henderson is trying to establish himself. Deni Avdija is trying to take a leap. One of those guys — probably Ja — will prove to be an odd fit that new head coach Micah Nori will need to navigate around to make this team click.

82. Sacramento wins 16 games (21.5 over/under), its fewest in franchise history.

83. Domantas Sabonis quietly asks for a trade. But he doesn't get moved due to a lack of strong offers on the market.

84. Darius Acuff has multiple 40-point games.

85. San Antonio wins 60 games (59.5 over/under), but does not return to the NBA Finals.

86. The three-guard lineup works, but it's not optimal, so De'Aaron Fox moves to the bench and becomes a super Sixth Man.

87. Dylan Harper wins Most Improved Player of the Year.

88. Victor Wembanyama wins the first MVP of his career, and he becomes just the fourth player in NBA history to win both MVP and Defensive Player of the Year in the same season. He would join Michael Jordan, Hakeem Olajuwon, and Giannis Antetokounmpo.

89. The Spurs become active in the trade market looking for an upgrade over Keldon Johnson and Tobias Harris.

90. Toronto wins 48 games (46.5 over/under).

91. Darko Rajaković wins Coach of the Year.

92. Jakob Poeltl is the weak link of the roster and the Raptors trade for a new center, but Rajaković navigates the challenges by leaning heavily on small ball with Collin Murray-Boyles playing a heavy dose of center.

93. Both Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes make All-NBA teams.

94. Utah wins 36 games (37.5 over/under).

95. Darryn Peterson plays 75 games, ending all concerns about his cramping that was experienced at Kansas. And in the process, he looks like a future star.

96. Keyonte George takes another leap, but just misses the cut for All-Star because players on teams winning more games get favored for the bench.

97. Mo Bamba proves himself as a serviceable backup center.

98. Washington wins 35 games (34.5 over/under), but misses the play-in tournament.

99. Touches become an issue for the youth. There will be too much Trae Young, and not enough AJ Dybantsa and Kyshawn George.

100. As a result, Dybantsa doesn't finish in the top three for Rookie of the Year voting. But he still resembles a future star with the opportunities provided despite having to share the ball so much. In the long run, maybe that ends up being for the best.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Opens Up About 'Darkest Time' in His NBA Career After Achilles Injury
articles.summary: Damian Lillard told Andscape's Marc J. Spears he struggled with a sense of being in "limbo" when the Milwaukee Bucks waived him shortly after he ruptured his left Achilles tendon in the spring of 2025.
articles.body:
Damian Lillard told Andscape's Marc J. Spears he struggled with a sense of being in "limbo" when the Milwaukee Bucks waived him shortly after he ruptured his left Achilles tendon in the spring of 2025.

Lillard suffered the Achilles injury in his final game with the Bucks during the first round of the 2025 playoffs.

He was cut from the team three months later, then spent two and a half weeks as a free agent before he re-signed with the Portland Trail Blazers.

The 10 Biggest Contract Extensions in NBA History 💸

"The darkest day was when I got when I was hurt and got waived," Lillard told Spears. "It wasn't a matter of, 'Am I going to get an opportunity?' It was just like, it was a possibility and a thought of mine. 'Well, do I just sit the year out and not be on the team and just wait until next summer when I'm healthy, and then go and visit teams and just work out for them and whatever and try to figure it out from there?' What do you do?

"And that was probably the darkest time, because I didn't really know which way I wanted to go. I would say when I got waived, and it was kind of like that limbo, and I had never not been on the team. I had a stretch of time where I just wasn't on the team."

Lillard has previously spoken about being surprised about the Bucks' decision to waive him just two seasons after acquiring him from the Trail Blazers, with which Lillard had spent 11 seasons before requesting a trade in 2023.

He told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel 's Jim Owczarski he had learned about the deal not through a conversation with the Bucks but via a social media post.

"I think that's the craziest part of it is I left here with four years on my deal and in my mind I was gonna be in Milwaukee the next four seasons at least," Lillard told Owczarski in July 2025. "And that was it. Things turn quickly from being hurt and then being waived unexpected and then obviously (Portland) coming as an aggressive suitor for me to come back."

The Bucks waived and stretched Lillard's former contract in order to sign Myles Turner as part of an ultimately failed bid to retain Giannis Antetokounmpo, who was traded to the Miami Heat in June.

Lillard sat out the entirety of last season amid his injury recovery. While Antetokounmpo prepares for his Heat debut, Lillard is getting ready to officially make his return to the Blazers Wednesday night against the visiting Phoenix Suns.

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns Says He's Willing to Take Knicks Pay Cut, Has Never Asked for Max Contract
articles.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns says he would be willing to take a pay cut in order to stay with the defending champion New York Knicks.
articles.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns says he would be willing to take a pay cut in order to stay with the defending champion New York Knicks.

In a joint interview with Finals MVP Jalen Brunson, Towns told ESPN's Malika Andrews he would accept less money on his next contract "because I want this team to stay together."

"That's always been my main priority was to keep everyone here, to keep this core, this special team that we have," Towns told Andrews. "So, it was the first thing on my mind... there was nowhere in my mind a max was even thought of."

The 10 Biggest Contract Extensions in NBA History 💸

Brunson followed up by telling Andrews he hoped Towns would "sign the contract."

Towns, 30, is heading into the final guaranteed year of his current contract under a $57 million cap hit. He holds a $61 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign.

He is eligible for a four-year, $276 million extension that would keep him in New York through the 2030-31 season, per ESPN .

Towns played a key role in the Knicks' run to the title, during which he averaged 15.9 points and 10.6 rebounds through 19 playoff games.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported in early October the Knicks' latest offer to Towns had been a four-year extension worth approximately $200 million deal.

Andrews previously reported on NBA Today Towns was willing to take a pay cut but felt the number the Knicks were asking for was "unreasonable."

Towns said before the Knicks' preseason the chances of him signing an extension before the regular season didn't "look good," per the New York Post 's Stefan Bondy .

When asked if he thought he should be rewarded for his role in helping the Knicks win a championship, Towns said, "No s- -t, Sherlock," per Bondy.

"Simply put: I want to do something to keep the team together and can work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said earlier this month, per Bondy. "And none of those things are close to happening."

The Knicks announced shortly afterward all contract talks would be paused "until later in the season."

Knicks governor James Dolan said this summer he is not willing to exceed the NBA's second luxury tax apron even if it was necessary to keep together the 2025 championship team, per ESPN's Vincent Goodwill .

The Knicks are currently projected to come in just under the second apron this season, per Spotrac .

Maintaining that status in the future will be difficult given the raises likely expected by multiple key members of the championship team.

Miles McBride, Josh Hart and Tyler Kolek are also currently eligible for extensions. Brunson, who took a pay cut on his last deal, becomes eligible for his own four-year, $257 million max extension next summer.

The Knicks have until June 30 to negotiate extensions with players like Towns, McBride, Hart and Kolek. Knicks president Leon Rose may need to decide which members of the championship team to prioritize as he looks to both stay under the second apron and continue building a contender around Brunson.

articles.title: Adam Silver fine with LeBron James' helicopter travel to Philadelphia: 'It's perfectly appropriate'
articles.summary: LeBron James has been traveling between New York and Philadelphia via a Fanatics helicopter ever since he signed with the 76ers.
articles.body:
Adam Silver is totally fine with LeBron James' helicopter use, as long as the Philadelphia 76ers aren't paying for it.

Silver said on Tuesday ahead of the NBA's opening day slate, that James using a helicopter to commute from New York to Philadelphia regularly is "perfectly appropriate."

"He has a deal with Fanatics," Silver said on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Tuesday . "It's perfectly appropriate if part of his deal is they're gonna supply a helicopter to him as long as it's just a deal between the Fanatics and LeBron and no team is involved. There's no rules issue there whatsoever."

James signed a deal to join the 76ers this past offseason, and he will start his record 24th season in the NBA on Tuesday when they take on the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden. But instead of finding a place to live in the Philadelphia area, James is instead living in New York and flying back and forth via helicopter.

That helicopter travel is part of James' deal with Fanatics, a sports platform known for its apparel business. James has been using their aviation after he signed a multi-year trading card partnership with the company in January 2024.

James described the trip , which is estimated to take between 30 to 45 minutes, as "just another way of transportation."

But the perk has drawn plenty of questions in the lead up to the 2026-27 season. James signed a very team-friendly deal with the 76ers — his two-year deal is only worth about $8 million — and Fanatics owner Michael Rubin was once a minority owner of the 76ers. Rubin sold his shares in 2022.

It's even drawn the attention of investigative journalist Pablo Torre, who told Front Office Sports recently that his team was "looking into all of the ways that this is both a good story as well as something that is of interest to the league." Torre, of course, broke the Kawhi Leonard-Clippers salary cap circumvention scandal.

But for James, the helicopter usage is simply just another part of his deal with Fanatics.

"The deal we signed with Fanatics almost three years ago includes access to their corporate aviation," a spokesperson for James said earlier this month. "It's a feature in many of their deals with their largest athletes and we appreciate their partnership as LeBron splits his time between New York and Philadelphia."

With Silver not bothered by the helicopter usage, and the 76ers not funding it, James is sure to keep flying back and forth throughout the season. Any conceived scandal here, those two clearly believe, is simply conjecture.

articles.title: Knicks' NBA Cup Banner Unveiled at MSG in Photo Ahead of Ceremony Celebrating 2026 Championship
articles.summary: The New York Knicks are officially acknowledging their 2025 NBA Cup championship now that the franchise has followed it up with an NBA title.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are officially acknowledging their 2025 NBA Cup championship now that the franchise has followed it up with an NBA title.

The Knicks raised their NBA Cup banner ahead of Tuesday's season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers, according to the New York Post 's Stefan Bondy.

The Knicks won the in-season tournament over the San Antonio Spurs in December.

SNY's Ian Begley reported shortly afterward the Knicks would not be raising an NBA Cup banner because of the franchise's focus on winning a title.

The Knicks are now expected to celebrate their June championship win over the Spurs with a ring ceremony and banner raising ahead of Tuesday's tip-off at Madison Square Garden, per Bondy .

The NBA Cup banner marks the first time the Knicks have commemorated an accomplishment in the Madison Square Garden rafters since winning a division title 2013.

The Los Angeles Lakers and Milwaukee Bucks each hung celebratory banners after winning the NBA's first two in-season tournaments, SNY's Alex Smith noted. Hall of Famer Reggie Miller later speculated the Lakers had been encouraged to hang the inaugural NBA Cup banner by commissioner Adam Silver.

Both of those previous NBA Cup victors went on to lose in the first round of their respective postseasons.

The Knicks mixed things up by celebrating their own in-season championship with a ceremony , but no banner-raising, ahead of a matchup against the Sixers last December.

The Spurs and Knicks went on to play an NBA Cup rematch in the NBA Finals in June.

Brunson, who was named the NBA Cup MVP in December, also earned the title of NBA Finals MVP after setting a franchise championship series record with 45 points in a title-clinching Game 5 win.

The Knicks will now celebrate that run by hanging their first championship banner since 1973 in a ceremony starting at 6:30 p.m. ET and broadcasting on NBC and Peacock.

LeBron James will then to make his Philadelphia 76ers debut as the visiting team looks to spoil the Knicks' banner night starting at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Knicks Reveal Gold-Themed Uniforms in Video for 2026 NBA Opener vs. LeBron James, 76ers
articles.summary: The defending NBA champion New York Knicks revealed gold-accented uniforms for their season opener on Tuesday evening at home versus the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
The defending NBA champion New York Knicks revealed gold-accented uniforms for their season opener on Tuesday evening at home versus the Philadelphia 76ers.

Sixers Out to Spoil Knicks' Ring Night 😈

The jerseys feature a championship patch above the last names, gold lettering and gold numbers. "Champs" is also embroidered in script on the jersey.

The Knicks won their first championship in 53 years. They went 16-3 in the playoffs, including a 15-1 stretch after falling behind two games to one to the Atlanta Hawks in the first round of the playoffs. New York then ripped off 12 straight wins, sweeping the Philadelphia 76ers and Cleveland Cavaliers in the process.

The Knicks beat the San Antonio Spurs in the first two games of the NBA Finals before dropping Game 3. However, the Knicks overcame a 29-point deficit in Game 4 to win 107-106 thanks in part to OG Anunoby's legendary tip-in.

New York then took Game 5 in San Antonio, 94-90, behind 45 points from Jalen Brunson.

The Knicks now hope to go back-to-back. They return all five of their starters and most of their bench, although the Knicks lost center Mitchell Robinson in free agency to the Boston Celtics. New York did add a capable big man in Andre Drummond to replace him in the rotation.

The Knicks have some tough competitors in the Eastern Conference, including the 76ers, Cleveland Cavaliers, Detroit Pistons and Boston Celtics. They'll first see Philadelphia, which added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown to a team that made the second round of the playoffs last season.

articles.title: Knicks Vs. 76ers Season Opener Breaks Decade-Old Record for Most Expensive Regular Season NBA Game Ever
articles.summary: The 2026-2027 NBA season kicks off tonight with the most expensive regular season game on record. The reigning champion New York Knicks are set to take on Le...
articles.body:
The 2026-2027 NBA season kicks off tonight with the most expensive regular season game on record.

The reigning champion New York Knicks are set to take on LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday, October 20. Add in the fact that the Knicks will receive their championship rings before the game, and you have the trifecta for sky-high ticket prices.

The highly-anticipated matchup — which is scheduled for a 7 p.m. tipoff — had a "get-in" price of around $2,000 on TickPick less than two hours earlier.

The game breaks a decade-old record previously held by the Los Angeles Lakers versus Utah Jazz game on April 13, 2016. Fans shelled out a whopping $1,137 to be in attendance for Kobe Bryant 's final game, Forbes reported.

James, 41, shocked the sports world when he announced he would be joining the Sixers for what will likely be his final seasons in the league. Tuesday marks his first time suiting up for the Philly team.

"I thought I was done when the season ended," he shared via X on July 24. "I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love this game."

He continued, "This is my last decision….I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time."

articles.title: Knicks Make James Wiseman Announcement Before Opening Night
articles.summary: The New York Knicks have a lot of their roster back from their NBA championship team. The center position is going to look different, though, behind Karl-Ant...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks have a lot of their roster back from their NBA championship team.

The center position is going to look different, though, behind Karl-Anthony Towns, because Mitchell Robinson has departed for the Boston Celtics.

The Knicks brought in a couple of veterans to potentially fill out the depth chart, and two made the team.

The first, and most likely to see sizable minutes, is Andre Drummond. The rebounding machine should be KAT's direct backup.

The other veteran who made the roster? James Wiseman.

Wiseman making the team was first made clear when the Knicks waived Bruce Brown over the weekend.

The final roster spot appeared to be down to Brown and Wiseman, and so when Brown was cut, that meant Wiseman would be on the Knicks.

Wiseman has also had his jersey number made official — he'll wear 35:

Shoutout to former Syracuse star Demetris Nichols as the last Knicks player to wear 35 before Wiseman.

Really, though, it's just remarkable that Wiseman continues to stick around the NBA. And as long as he's hanging around, there will still be people who believe in him.

Wiseman put up 18 points and 10 rebounds to end the preseason. If the Knicks needed to see a statement from him to make the roster, that certainly applied.

The intrigue surrounding Wiseman might've been enough all by itself, though, to keep him around at least for a little while.

Wiseman was the No. 1 high school recruit in the country in the Class of 2019, and even after a bumpy season eligibility-wise at Memphis, he was the No. 2 overall pick in the 2020 NBA Draft by the Golden State Warriors .

The big lefty did get a ring with Golden State, but he never found a way to thrive there. He has since played for the Detroit Pistons and Indiana Pacers — although injuries limited him to just five games in two seasons with the Pacers.

Now, Wiseman has found his way to the Big Apple, where it's not clear if he'll see much playing time.

Amazingly, Wiseman is still just 25 years old. You'll find Knicks fans who have talked themselves into believing that Wiseman can be a real contributor to this roster.

And hey, maybe he can — a guy who once had the hype of Wiseman will always feel like a player you can dream on, even if he's come up short so far in his NBA career.

articles.title: Jaxon Kohler receives injunction, will remain eligible for BYU
articles.summary: The former Michigan State big man is expected to be key contributor for this year’s Cougars.
articles.body:
BYU's last hurdle before the regular season has been cleared.

Big man Jaxon Kohler will remain eligible for the Cougars, as a California court granted his preliminary injunction Tuesday for a fifth season of college eligibility.

The news was first reported by Robby McCombs of Vanquish the Foe . According to CBS Sports college basketball insider Jon Rothstein, the NCAA will appeal the ruling.

As previously reported by the Deseret News , Kohler's effort to receive further eligibility came in the aftermath of the NCAA's new "five in five" eligibility model, which was not originally grandfathered to him as a class of 2022 high school graduate.

Kohler, along with more than 70 other athletes, was granted a temporary restraining order against the NCAA in August as part of Glancey v. NCAA, allowing him to enter the transfer portal and land at BYU .

The preliminary hearing for Glancey v. NCAA began in September and concluded Tuesday. The granted injunction means Kohler will remain eligible at least through the final trial date, which has yet to be determined.

A four-year contributor at Michigan State who earned All-Big Ten honors last season, Kohler recorded a double-double of 10 points and 10 points in BYU's preseason exhibition against Nebraska this past Friday, leading coach Kevin Young to call him "the perfect fit" at center for the Cougars.

"It felt amazing, it felt surreal," Kohler said after the Nebraska exhibition. "I mean, to play with these guys, to play for the community I was raised in and to go out there and be a Cougar, man, it was really special, to be honest."

articles.title: Texas A&M guard granted preliminary injunction for 2026-27 eligibility
articles.summary: Texas A&M basketball received massive news regarding the status of a Texas transfer guard's preliminary injunction against the NCAA on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Texas A&M basketball just received a massive update regarding the status of a Texas transfer guard's preliminary injunction against the NCAA.

According to a report from TexAgs ' basketball analyst and insider Luke Evangelist , Aggie guard Jordan Pope's preliminary injunction was granted by California on Tuesday, marking a longer-term protection for his eligibility. It is a huge win for Texas A&M and second-year head coach Bucky McMillan as tipoff to the 2026-27 season looms closer.

While the war against the NCAA for gaining full eligibility is not over for Pope and many other college basketball athletes from the class of 2022, the battle has seemingly been won. The NCAA will appeal the judge's ruling, which could mean another court date being established before the season ends, but the odds of the talented guard playing a large chunk of the upcoming campaign grew much larger with this week's decision in California.

Pope spent the first two years of his collegiate career at Oregon State before transferring to Texas and playing the last two seasons with the Longhorns. He averaged 13.1 points and 1.9 assists in 29.0 minutes for Sean Miller's squad in 2025-26 and played a huge role in the program's historic run to the Sweet 16.

The former Texas guard is already making waves as one of the most impressive shooters on the floor in Texas A&M's recent scrimmages and open practices. Pope's attributes and consistency from range are a perfect fit for McMillan's high-paced, volume-shooting approach, which made a splash in the program's run to the Round of 32 in the NCAA Tournament last season.

There may not be any more Rashaun Agee, but having shooters like Pope, PJ Haggerty and other electrifying scorers on the roster is a major advantage for the Aggies.

articles.summary: Come one, come all, you're just in time to witness the New York Knicks take on the Philadelphia 76ers to open the 2026-27 NBA season!
articles.body:
Come one, come all, you're just in time to witness the New York Knicks take on the Philadelphia 76ers to open the 2026-27 NBA season!

How will the Knicks play on the night they receive their championship rings? What do LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look like in their official Sixers debuts? And how does Philly's starting unit with them, Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe fare after playing only once together in the preseason?

There's plenty more to follow. Keep it right here as we break down the biggest storylines, highlights, strategies and takeaways throughout the game below.
